questions.question: Newton's forward difference formula is applied to tabulated equal-interval values of $y$ in order to (a) extrapolate from the beginning of the table (b) extrapolate from the end of the table (c) interpolate anywhere in the table (d) differentiate the function
questions.solution:
Newton's forward formula is
$$y(x)=y_{0}+p\Delta y_{0}+\frac{p(p-1)}{2!}\Delta^{2}y_{0}+\frac{p(p-1)(p-2)}{3!}\Delta^{3}y_{0}+\cdots,\qquad p=\frac{x-x_{0}}{h}$$
Here $y_{0}$ is the **first** value in the table and the differences are built forward from it, so the method is efficient when $x$ lies near $x_{0}$ — i.e. at the beginning of the tabulation. (For values near the end, one uses the **backward** difference formula.)

**Correct option: (a)**
questions.knowledgeNote: Newton's forward formula starts from $y_{0}$ (first tabulated value); near the end of the table use the backward formula instead.
